title: Compactness and Continuity Scaffold for the Loomis Route
body_html:
Compactness and Continuity Scaffold for the Loomis Route

For a finite index type $I$, the real standard simplex $\Delta(I) = \mathrm{stdSimplex}\ \mathbb{R}\ I$ is a compact metric subspace of $I \to \mathbb{R}$ (Mathlib supplies the stdSimplex.instCompactSpace_coe instance directly).

This node packages the simplex-side companion facts that the simplified-Loomis proof of the minimax theorem relies on:

  1. Point-mass strategies. For any $i_0 \in I$, the indicator $e_{i_0} \in \Delta(I)$ has $e_{i_0}(i) = 1$ if $i = i_0$ and $0$ otherwise. Weighted sums against $e_{i_0}$ evaluate the chosen coordinate.
  2. Pointwise-to-weighted bound transfer. A function $f \colon I \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $f(i) \ge v$ for every $i$ iff its weighted sum $\sum_i x_i f(i)$ is $\ge v$ for every $x \in \Delta(I)$; the analogous statement for $\le$ holds as well.
  3. Continuity of weighted sums. Each coordinate projection $x \mapsto x(i)$ on $\Delta(I)$ is continuous, and so is the weighted-sum functional $x \mapsto \sum_i x(i) f(i)$ for any fixed $f$.
proof_html:
The point-mass strategy is the obvious zero/one indicator function; its weighted sum is a single nonzero term. The transfer statements follow by inserting the point mass $e_{i_0}$ to recover the pointwise bound, and by dominating the weighted sum with $\sum_i x_i v = v$ in the converse direction. Continuity of coordinate projection is continuous_apply composed with the subtype-value map, and the weighted sum is a finite sum of products of continuous functions.

References

  • [MFoGT, Chapter 2, Section 2.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Topological setup for the LRS Loomis-style minimax proof.
